purpose.description: Measure how repeated stochastic observations reduce estimation uncertainty after factorization has been established.
purpose.role: Separate stochastic estimation limits from interface-level identifiability failures.
not_used_for: replacing factorization existence with statistical confidence
treating more samples as an interface refinement

system_class.description: Stochastic systems where observations are distributions rather than deterministic outputs.

observation_operator.definition: Induced observation distribution generated by system f.

stochastic_factorization.interpretation: Distribution-level observation equivalence must preserve target value.

metric.name: target_estimation_error
metric.description: Mean deviation between estimated target and true target after n repetitions.

curve_analysis.interpretation: Repeated sampling reduces uncertainty but does not change whether the target factors through the interface.

factorization.question: Does a target function exist over the observation distribution?

estimation.question: How accurately can the target function be learned from finite samples?

boundary_checks.claim: Infinite samples can rescue a non-identifiable interface
boundary_checks.reason: Sampling cannot separate identical observation distributions.

boundary_checks.claim: One observation is enough whenever factorization exists
boundary_checks.reason: Finite samples may still produce high estimation variance.
Poor estimation can occur after successful factorization.

decision.meaning: Stochastic repetition reduces uncertainty only after interface-level identifiability exists.

notes: The repetition curve begins only after the interface proof.
Finite samples estimate a factorized target; they do not create factorization.
The hierarchy remains: interface existence -> estimation -> prediction.
